page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-32 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c4 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz and is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache. It includes 248.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1933.0 and strong results in image and text processing. Multi-core performance is balanced, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 15636.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 47956.79. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2186.0 GB/sec, while large block uncached read and write speeds reach 144.63 GB/sec and 61.79 GB/sec respectively. In specialized workloads, the instance achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 421.19 tokens/sec for small 135M LLM models, though performance drops to 2.38 tokens/sec for large 70B models. Static web serving throughput is strong at 51.15 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-32 provides a dense allocation of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The presence of advanced CPU instruction sets, such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), enhances its efficiency for vector and matrix operations without the overhead of dedicated accelerators. This instance is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, static web serving, and small-scale language model inference.
